topic: using silence as leverage in an argument or negotiation
title: Why Silence Makes People Blink First
description: AI-narrated commentary: why staying quiet after the hardest thing you say is one of the most effective psychological moves in an argument or negotiation -- and why almost no one can hold it. #psychology #shorts

hook_candidates.text: Go quiet after the hard part, and most people can't stand it -- they'll blink first.
Why do skilled negotiators go dead silent right after they say the hardest thing?
Staying calm in an argument isn't about hiding your feelings -- it's a tactic that makes the other person cave first.
Trained negotiators are taught to let the silence sit -- the longer it stretches, the more the other side gives away.

beats.text: Go quiet after the hard part, and most people can't stand it — they'll **blink** first.
**Silence** breaks the rule that a question gets an answer — so they rush to fill the gap.
Don't fill silence — **blink** less than they do. What's your record? Comment it below.
